questions.question: Utility is SUBJECTIVE, meaning:
options: It lives in the user, not the object — the same umbrella is priceless in a storm and useless on a clear day

questions.question: Value in use and value in exchange differ in that:
options: Use-value is how useful a thing is to its owner; exchange-value is what it can fetch when traded
Exchange value applies only to exports
Use value is measured in money

questions.question: The water-diamond paradox resolves because exchange value is governed by:
options: SCARCITY relative to wants, and the utility of the NEXT unit — plenty cheapens, scarcity dearens

questions.question: Price is best defined as:
options: Value in EXCHANGE expressed in money — one language for all worths

questions.question: The perfect market's conditions include:
options: Many buyers and sellers, homogeneous product, perfect knowledge, free entry and exit
One seller, unique product, secret prices

questions.question: Under perfect conditions, every participant is a:
options: PRICE TAKER — the market's crossing point sets the price; each simply accepts it

questions.question: Banks, cellphone networks and fuel companies exemplify:
options: OLIGOPOLY — a few large sellers, each watching the others, often competing on everything except price

questions.question: Restaurants and hair salons — many sellers of similar but differentiated services — are:
options: MONOPOLISTIC COMPETITION — each with small pricing power carved out by brand, location or style

subtopics.title: World Markets and the Effects of Electronics

questions.question: "The platinum price is set by global buying and selling, not in Rustenburg" illustrates:
options: WORLD MARKETS — global prices as domestic realities for a commodity exporter

questions.question: The farmer checking the produce-market price before the middleman arrives shows electronics:
options: Brightening KNOWLEDGE — prices visible to anyone with a phone strengthen the weaker negotiator

questions.question: The seamstress selling through a social-media page shows electronics:
options: LOWERING ENTRY BARRIERS — entering the clothing market without a shopfront

questions.question: The balanced verdict on electronic markets:
options: Wider, faster, better informed — but platform power, world competition and the digital divide mean not automatically FAIRER

questions.question: The five functions of markets are:
options: Price formation, allocation, information, rationing, linking buyers and sellers

questions.question: Prices allocate resources by:
options: STEERING factors of production — rising prices signal producers to make more, drawing labour and capital toward what society wants

questions.question: "One number carries news about scarcity, costs, tastes and expectations to everyone at once" describes:
options: The INFORMATION function — prices as compressed messages

questions.question: The critical footnote to the five functions:
options: Markets serve those WITH buying power — where need lacks income or costs land on third parties, state intervention enters

subtopics.title: Why Water Costs R25 at the Stadium

questions.question: The same bottle costing R7 outside and R25 inside the stadium shows:
options: Utility lives in YOU — thirst, heat and locked gates changed the satisfaction, not the water
A government tax at the gates

questions.question: Water beats diamonds in usefulness-worth but loses in trading-worth because:
options: Trading-worth runs on SCARCITY — plenty makes cheap, scarce makes dear, regardless of nobility

questions.question: The stadium "proves the rule in reverse" because:
options: Locking the gates made water inside SCARCE — and its price tripled

subtopics.title: The Potato Market and the Phone Shops

questions.question: At the dawn potato market, charging double fails because:
options: Buyers simply step to the next stall — no single seller can budge the one going price

questions.question: The three streetwise sorting questions are:
options: Who owns it, who runs it, who shops there?
How many sellers; identical or dressed-up-different products; how easily can a newcomer set up?
Cash or credit; local or imported; old or new?
Big or small; rich or poor; urban or rural?

questions.question: The company with the only patented pill is:
options: A MONOPOLY — one seller, no substitutes, a price maker bounded only by what buyers can bear

questions.question: The street of hair salons holds "small pricing power" because:
options: Each is a little DIFFERENT — braids, location, vibe — carving out loyal customers: monopolistic competition

questions.question: The farmer checking prices before the middleman arrives now negotiates from:
options: KNOWLEDGE — the phone moved 'perfect knowledge' from textbook fiction toward daily fact

questions.question: The "new kind of locked gate" in electronic markets is:
options: The DIGITAL DIVIDE — those without data stand outside the electronic market entirely

questions.question: "Markets make prices, and prices do the rest" compresses:
options: The five functions — formation first, then allocation, information, rationing and connection all flowing from the price

questions.question: The chain linking the coffee farmer to your cup demonstrates:
options: The LINKING function — markets connect strangers across the globe who need never meet
